sections.h2: What are my choices if I want to sell a house in Paramus quickly?
sections.html:
A Paramus owner can list with an agent, sell privately, or accept a cash offer from a buyer who takes the house as it stands. Each route still ends at the same borough inspection and the same state deed filings, so the real difference is how much preparation you do before closing.

Paramus is a borough in central Bergen County, roughly 15 to 20 miles northwest of Midtown Manhattan. The borough is best known for its two retail corridors along Routes 4 and 17, yet it is also a suburban bedroom community of New York City. Before you pick a route, work through this short list:

  • Check whether any permit for past work on the house is still open at the Building Department.
  • Decide whether you can wait for a conventional buyer's financing and inspection period.
  • Gather the deed, mortgage payoff figure and any estate paperwork if the owner has died.
  • Ask a closing attorney which deed forms the sale needs.

A direct cash sale shortens the marketing stage. It does not remove the borough's Certificate of Compliance, which Paramus describes as mandatory for real estate closings.

sections.h2: What is it like to own and sell a home in Paramus?
sections.html:
Paramus covers 10.5 square miles and was incorporated in April 1922 after it split off from Midland Township, which is now Rochelle Park. It was farm country until the 1950s, when the George Washington Bridge and wider Routes 4 and 17 pulled in shopping centers. Garden State Plaza sits where those two routes cross, and the Census Bureau reports 2022 retail sales in the borough of about $5.45 billion.

The borough names five residential areas: Arcola, Bergen Place, Dunkerhook, Fairway Oaks and Spring Valley. Van Saun County Park (146 acres, with the county zoo) lies on the east side, and Saddle River County Park runs along the west side with a six-mile bike path. Paramus Public Schools run eight schools from pre-kindergarten through grade 12, and Bergen Community College has its main campus in the borough.

Getting around is mostly by car. The borough counts 121.92 miles of road, including Route 17, Route 4 and Garden State Parkway Interchange 165, and NJ Transit buses reach the Port Authority Bus Terminal and the George Washington Bridge Bus Station. Sellers who live near the highways should expect buyers to ask about traffic noise and commute time, since the Census puts the mean trip to work at 30.8 minutes.

sections.h2: What do Census figures say about Paramus homes and households?
sections.html:
Paramus is a high-value, owner-heavy market, with more than four in five homes lived in by their owners. The figures below come straight from the Census Bureau and describe the borough as a whole, not any one street.

One in four residents is 65 or older, and many longtime owners are weighing downsizing or handling a parent's home. If that describes your situation, the estate and tax pointers further down matter as much as the price.

sections.h2: What does Paramus require before my house can close?
sections.html:
Paramus requires a Certificate of Compliance for any resale or rental, and the borough states that this certificate is mandatory for closings. The Building Department asks sellers to confirm first that every earlier permit has been closed out, then file an application with a $100 fee for a sale.

After the application is accepted, an inspector visits. Resale inspections run weekday mornings from 9:00 to 12:00, and someone needs to be at the house to let the inspector in. The borough's guidelines list what gets checked:

  • Smoke alarms on every level and near bedrooms, plus carbon monoxide detectors near sleeping areas, following the borough's NFPA-based guidelines.
  • A permanent label within 18 inches of the electrical panel and meter if the house has solar panels, a generator or battery storage.
  • The street number visible from the street on the mailbox, front door or garage.
  • Borough-issued garbage and recycling containers on the property with their serial numbers.
  • A fence around any pool.

Open permits cause the most delays. Work done without a permit has to be applied for and inspected before the certificate is released, and permitted work without a final inspection holds up the Certificate of Occupancy. The guidelines ask that all open permits be closed at least one week before the resale inspection is scheduled. Call the Building Department at 201-265-2100, extension 2230, for the current process.

sections.h2: What will I pay the state when I sell a Paramus house?
sections.html:
New Jersey puts the Realty Transfer Fee on the seller, collected when the deed is recorded. It is a bracketed rate per $500 of the price, and for sales above $350,000 the schedule starts at $2.90 per $500 on the first $150,000 and climbs to $6.05 per $500 above $1,000,000. Sales over $1,000,000 also carry a supplemental Graduated Percent Fee that the seller owes by statute.

Some transfers qualify for exemptions, such as a deed from an executor to an heir under a will or intestacy, or a deed between a parent and child. Anyone claiming a full or partial exemption files the Affidavit of Consideration for Use by Seller, Form RTF-1, with the deed. Ask the closing attorney or title agent for the exact dollar figure on your deed.

A separate Gross Income Tax form, GIT/REP, is recorded with the deed under N.J.S.A. 54A:8-9. Its job is to tell the State whether a nonresident seller must prepay estimated income tax. The person signing the deed completes it, and only sheriff's sales and bankruptcy trustee sales are excused from filing.

sections.h2: Do I have to disclose flood risk when I sell in Paramus?
sections.html:
Yes. Since March 20, 2024, every New Jersey seller must give the buyer flood information in the property condition disclosure statement before the buyer is bound by the contract. That includes whether the property sits in FEMA's Special Flood Hazard Area or Moderate Flood Hazard Area and anything you actually know about flooding on the lot.

The Department of Environmental Protection runs a Flood Risk Notification Tool that helps sellers look up the answers. Check your own parcel on that tool instead of assuming the answer. Cash buyers and conventional buyers receive the same disclosure.

sections.h2: How do property taxes and appeals work for a Paramus owner?
sections.html:
New Jersey assesses every parcel at 100 percent of true market value, using an October 1 assessment date, and your tax bill is the local rate times that assessed value. Paramus homes sit in Bergen County, so an assessment appeal goes to the Bergen County Board of Taxation.

  • The petition must be received, not just mailed, by April 1 of the tax year.
  • If the borough has done a revaluation or reassessment, the deadline is May 1.
  • Owners with an assessment above $1,000,000 may go straight to the State Tax Court.
  • A county board decision can be appealed to the Tax Court within 45 days.

You must show the assessment is out of line with market value or with the common level range for the district. Ask the Paramus tax collector for your payoff and quarterly status before closing, so any open installment is cleared at the closing table and the buyer inherits no surprise.

faqs.q: Is a borough certificate really required to close a sale in Paramus?
faqs.a: Yes. Paramus calls its Certificate of Compliance for resale mandatory for real estate closings. The seller applies to the Building Department, pays $100 and passes an inspection.

faqs.q: What happens if I made changes to the house without permits?
faqs.a: The resale certificate is withheld until the missing permits are applied for and the work is inspected. Permitted work that never received a final inspection holds up the Certificate of Occupancy.

faqs.q: Who pays the New Jersey Realty Transfer Fee?
faqs.a: The seller. The State imposes it on the seller when the deed is recorded, and the amount follows the price brackets in the Division of Taxation schedule.

faqs.q: When does flood information have to be given to a buyer?
faqs.a: Before the buyer becomes obligated under the purchase contract. Sellers disclose FEMA flood zone status and any flood problems they know about on the property condition disclosure statement.

faqs.q: What is the last day to appeal my Paramus assessment?
faqs.a: April 1, or May 1 if the borough carried out a revaluation or reassessment. The county board must receive the petition by that day. Ask the Bergen County Board of Taxation for the form and current filing steps.
